Getting Started > Mobile Transpilation: sla2swift and sla2kotlin
Status: direction ruling record (2026-10-29, decided by the user). This page registers the route ruling for writing Android / iOS in SLA (adopting dual transpilers) and its form constraints; the design census is under way, and the details follow the census output. This direction is a side track; the master ordering is in section nine of document 13 and section four of document 17.

1. The Requirement: Artifacts Are Delivered to Clients, and Clients Use Only Swift / Kotlin

Decided by the user (2026-10-29): besides writing frontends and backends, SLA must also be able to write Android / iOS directly. The decisive constraint is not technical but in the delivery form: mobile artifacts are delivered to clients, and the clients explicitly want to use the two languages Swift and Kotlin and are not familiar with SA / SLA. That is, the clients must receive the artifacts in the source form of these two languages and continue maintaining them within their own toolchains (Xcode / Android Studio); delivering an intermediate form they cannot read does not work.

2. Three Routes and the Ruling: A and B Rejected, C Adopted

  • A — SA native compilation to arm64 + a thin C ABI glue layer (rejected). SLA is compiled via SA to native arm64 artifacts, exposed through a C ABI, with a thin glue layer written on the host side to connect to the platform. This route makes the clients face something other than Swift / Kotlin source, so the delivery form does not meet the constraints of section one.
  • B — Via SA's C emitter (rejected). The artifact is C source, which the client side then bridges into Swift / Kotlin. The clients explicitly want the two languages themselves; interposing a layer of C likewise does not meet the delivery form.
  • C — The sla2swift + sla2kotlin dual transpilers (adopted). SLA source is transpiled directly into Swift source and Kotlin source, and the clients receive and co-maintain it in native project form. Routes A and B were proposed by the main session's analysis and explicitly negated by the user on 2026-10-29; the only previously established case for C in this ecosystem was exactly "the artifact must be distributed as source in the target language", and mobile is precisely that case.

3. Form Constraints

  • Emission level: both transpilers take as input the AST after SLA checking (preferably after monomorphization), of the same origin as the existing text / SAB dual codegen; they do not go through the SA register layer (the register layer's form cannot produce target-language source that clients can read and maintain).
  • Loud rejection where there is no faithful mapping: wherever SLA semantics (ownership and moves, goroutine concurrency, etc.) have no faithful counterpart in Swift / Kotlin, the transpilers explicitly error and reject; silent approximation is forbidden — the lesson of the tsgosa dialect lies exactly here (surface conversions that look equivalent while the semantics quietly change). The rejection list is circled item by item by the design census and written down, leaving no implicit behavior.
  • The target-language runtime support surface: SLA concepts such as String, Vec and collections, and concurrency primitives are carried on the target side by a set of runtime support code delivered with the transpilers (one set each for Swift / Kotlin); the transpiled artifacts depend on this surface rather than being inlined expansion by expansion; the support surface's scope and form are defined by the design census.

4. Status and Schedule

The design census line has been dispatched: it will produce the mapping tables, unsupported lists, and phasing suggestions for sla2swift / sla2kotlin (stored in ~/workspace/sla2mobile/DESIGN.md), and its completion status follows its final report. This direction is positioned as a side track: the whole program's master ordering (the Erlang + goroutine complex → the three machines' concurrency performance improvements → Verse / Haskell features) is unchanged, and until the user promotes it separately, this line only registers the design census and does not take construction surface away from the main line.

Related discussions: cpp2sa and go2sa: Proposal Discussion for Two New Frontends (the opposite direction: there, other languages come into SA; here, SLA goes out to target languages), The goroutine Runtime: Design Discussion on Bringing It into sa_std (a source of the concurrency semantics, and one of the mapping difficulties).

Follow-up (evening of 2026-10-29): the master judgment across this direction and the two side tracks SAX cross-platform and sla2ts, the user's ruling chain, and the full register of the underlying deficiencies dug up (43 entries) are in document 19, "Side-Track Research and Low-Level Gap Register".
